newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo ad agency hires Coca-Cola executive.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo ad agency hires Coca-Cola executive.

text.p: Pepsi may have scored a point in its perennial battle against Coke -- at least in the European marketing arena.
Coca-Cola Co's marketing director in Europe, David Wheldon, resigned to join BBDO Worldwide, the advertising agency for rival PepsiCo, BBDO said Thursday.
Wheldon had just been promoted to the European post on October 1. Previously, he was director of advertising for Coca-Cola at its Atlanta headquarters.
As president of BBDO Europe, Wheldon will oversee the agency's business in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

BBDO Chairman and Chief Executive Allen Rosenshine said Wheldon was not joining the agency "to work on Pepsi but rather to work with all our European multinational clients on the globalization of their brands.
"Our Pepsi client had no involvement whatsoever in the hiring," he added.
Coca-Cola spokesman Bob Bertini said Wheldon's departure had nothing to do with the bottling wars.
"It was a personal career decision," Bertini said. "As with any business, people leave from time to time to pursue other opportunities."
Coca-Cola said it would name a replacement for Wheldon in Europe soon. In Atlanta, his former deputy, Ian Rowden, succeeded him as advertising director.

"I have done the advertising job I was hired to do at Coca-Cola, which allowed me to work with a variety of agencies around the world," Wheldon said in a statement. "I feel I've learned an immense amount, but now I want to return to the agency business ..."
BBDO's clients in Europe include Apple Computer Inc, Bayer AG, CPC International Inc, Gillette Co, Henkel KGaA, Mars, Sara Lee Corp, Wella AG and Wrigley.
